response: No, biochemical markers of bone turnover are not always representative of bone histomorphometry in postmenopausal women. While biochemical markers can provide information on the rate of bone resorption and formation, they may not accurately reflect the complex processes of bone remodeling and histological changes that occur at the tissue level, as assessed by bone histomorphometry. Studies have shown that there can be discrepancies between biochemical markers and histomorphometric parameters, highlighting the need for a comprehensive assessment of bone health in postmenopausal women.
